title: How can shoe sizes be put in order?
description: A teacher noted the shoe sizes of students on the board in no special order. The video arranges nine of those sizes in ascending order and reads the smallest and the largest, while Keeko doubts whether each size should be written only once.
teaching_notes: One idea: ascending order runs from the smallest to the largest, and a repeated value is written as many times as it occurs. Watch for children who write each size once and lose the count.

video_script.why: The child sees that ordering keeps every entry and puts equal sizes side by side.
video_script.substitution: the first row of the book's shoe-size data, nine students
video_script.anchor: Jia with the shoe sizes of students written on the board
video_script.wrong_answer: each size is written only once
video_script.wrong_move: writes each different size once and drops the repeated entries
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest size is three and the largest size is five.

names.Jia: teacher who records and orders the shoe sizes of her students

never_show: the whole class data of 27 sizes
answers about size 5 or larger than 4 in the class
maths_rules: First row of the book's data: 4 5 3 4 3 4 5 5 4, nine students.
Size 3 occurs 2 times, size 4 occurs 4 times, size 5 occurs 3 times.
video_script.design: Nine shoe sizes on the board; they slide into ascending order, equal sizes landing side by side.

beats.on_screen: title card with a teacher at the board and nine shoe sizes written in a jumbled row: 4 5 3 4 3 4 5 5 4

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the teacher
marks.sizes: the nine shoe sizes are written across the board
marks.ask: a question mark lights up above the row

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book, where Jia asked students their shoe sizes.
<bookmark mark='sizes'/>Nine of the sizes were written on the board in no special order.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we put them in order and read the smallest and the largest?

beats.on_screen: the jumbled row of sizes and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a card shows a row of sizes growing from the smallest on the left to the largest on the right, labelled ascending order

marks.grow: the sizes line up from the smallest to the largest
marks.name: the words ascending order are written under the row

narration: <bookmark mark='grow'/>Putting values from the smallest to the largest is called ascending order.
<bookmark mark='name'/>In this order, equal values sit side by side.
The smallest value comes first, and the largest comes last.

beats.on_screen: Given: shoe sizes of nine students: 4, 5, 3, 4, 3, 4, 5, 5, 4

marks.given: the nine sizes are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the shoe sizes of nine students: four, five, three, four, three, four, five, five, four.

beats.on_screen: To find: the sizes in ascending order, and the smallest and the largest

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the sizes in ascending order and name the smallest and the largest.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the smallest size is 3, worn by 2 students: 3, 3

marks.smallest: the two entries of size 3 slide to the front of a new row

narration: <bookmark mark='smallest'/>Step one, find the smallest size. It is three, and two students wear it.
Write three, three.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the next size is 4, worn by 4 students: 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4

marks.next: the four entries of size 4 slide in after the 3s

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step two, the next size is four, and four students wear it.
Write four, four, four, four after the threes.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the last size is 5, worn by 3 students: 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5

marks.last: the three entries of size 5 slide in at the end

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step three, the last size is five, and three students wear it.
Write five, five, five at the end.

marks.check: the entries are counted in the row and match the nine students

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, count the entries to check them.
Two and four and three make nine, so no size was lost.

marks.ans: the first and last entries of the row are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The smallest size is three and the largest size is five.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a row of only three entries, 3, 4, 5, with a cross over it, and the nine-entry row below it with a tick

marks.doubt: the short row of three entries appears and is crossed out
marks.fix: the row of nine entries appears with a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each size is written only once, so the list is three, four, five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But nine students wear shoes, so the list must have nine entries.
A size worn by four students is written four times.
